title: Surprised, it’s pretty solid.
body: I’ve spent some time using OpenClaw and Odysseus, and Muse is a fitting name for this product as it certainly is taking the literal definition and using it. It you’ve used either of those, you know what you’re getting into with a lot of the hard edges rounded off. There is a lack of control, but what is provided isn’t half bad, in fact I think it’s better in many aspects. You’re not thinking about models and if it should be done locally or handed off, it is the ‘just works’ kind of product. I have a few crons running for things I want to do, nothing extraordinary, but it’s been good at keeping up with updating spreadsheets and hasn’t face planted on anything yet, it finds and corrects mistakes while communicating that it made a mistake (good!) and I’ve had a couple of moments when it took an additional step that was actually useful. Full disclosure: I am paying for the $15/mo plan and decided that I wanted to from the start to get more compute to chew through and am using it. I hope that this level of function does not get trimmed later, praying to Moore for some of his law to come through here. It’s not all sunshine and rainbows, tracking usage is non-existent, you just have a ‘you’ve used this much’ meter. The Main Chat if you do not quickly stop using it will turn into a compute dump as it’s keeping it all in memory. I’ve moved to Side Chats for everything and we have a rule to ‘clear and refresh’ the chat with a quick memory job once we hit a quota of usage, all of this kind of culling should be automatic with a synopsis/memory/whatever to catch things up. Meta should likely look into building their own stack of Docs/Sheets/etc and at least have it as a free workspace with like 50mb on free plan and 2GB on first paid tier to get people to use the more cool things, I’d really like to see better onboarding to show how memory works, how to build rulesets into crons, etc. There is a ton of stuff you can do that’s just not documented or laid out to the user. I have started recommending this to friends and family members that are reluctant to use ‘AI stuff’. Seriously impressed, great job Meta, don’t stop. This is the new Horizon. :-)

title: An Incredible AI Tool with One Wish
body: Muse is one of those products that makes you realize just how powerful AI can be when it’s put to good use. I work in industrial equipment sales, engineering, and project management, and Muse has become an incredibly valuable tool for organizing ideas, developing strategies, and getting real work accomplished. My biggest complaint isn’t the product. It’s the cost. It seems like everything these days requires another monthly subscription, and those expenses add up quickly. I genuinely wish Muse offered a one-time lifetime purchase with unlimited access. I would gladly consider making that investment because I believe in this product, see its long-term potential, and want to support the people developing it. I understand that continued development and AI technology cost money, but I also believe there is a huge market of professionals like me who would rather invest once in a product they trust than worry about another recurring payment or future price increase. My message to the Muse team: Keep improving what you’re building, keep it affordable, and remember the customers who believe in your vision. Give us an opportunity to become lifetime supporters. Muse has earned my five stars. I just hope its pricing remains accessible as the product continues to grow.

More importantly, I used the Connectors in Muse one of which is Plaid. Plaid connects to your financial institution for Read Only access and I found out that my credit card debt is abominable. More importantly, Muse gave me a rundown on the automatic monthly charges on one of my credit cards (streaming services, subscriptions, etc) and I hadn’t realized that some of the products that I thought I cancelled actually were still being charged to my card (!) because I didn’t cancel it correctly. Muse was able to create a document for me to show the breakdown of the charges. I know that there are negative reviews, but honestly, I think that they “don’t get it” or they don’t trust AI. What I DO know is that it has helped me immeasurably. I have subscribed to the “Power” level. It’s $20 per month ($240 for the year) and worth every penny. Muse is *NOT* a “ChatGPT” type AI or a “Gemini”… it’s WAY better. Don’t listen to the naysayers who bash on Zuckerberg for his company’s creation of this wonderful tool. Visit the Reviews section, and see that there are approximately 400,000 (!) reviews and counting and the rating average is 4.9 stars!! That is saying something right there!!! Try it… there is a Free Version (no strings attached) and you just might find it to be a super time saver like I did.
